plugin_desc: Huawei-specific SNMP collection for switches. In addition to standard IF-MIB interface metrics, it collects Huawei private OIDs (HUAWEI-ENTITY-EXTENT-MIB) for device health: per-entity CPU/memory (descr=entPhysicalName), temperature sensors, fan status, and per-module SFP optical DDM (Rx/Tx power). Optical power is stored as raw µW; metrics keep module-level series (dimensions=descr) and convert to dBm in the query via 10*log10(µW/1000). Huawei reports memory as a utilization percentage directly and does not expose a power-supply state OID in this template. Supported brands/models — Huawei S-series campus switches (S5700/S6700/S7700/S9300, etc.) and CloudEngine CE series.
name: Switch

metrics.name: device_cpu_usage
metrics.description: Per-entity CPU utilization of the Huawei device control plane (HUAWEI-ENTITY-EXTENT-MIB hwEntityCpuUsage), normalized to a 0-100 percentage. Dimension descr is entPhysicalName. Sustained high CPU usage can indicate control-plane overload, routing instability, or attack traffic, and may lead to slow management response or packet processing delays.

metrics.name: device_memory_usage
metrics.description: Per-entity memory utilization of the Huawei device (HUAWEI-ENTITY-EXTENT-MIB hwEntityMemUsage), reported directly as a 0-100 percentage. Dimension descr is entPhysicalName. High memory usage may indicate memory leaks, oversized routing/MAC/ARP tables, or insufficient capacity, and can cause instability or failed allocations.

metrics.name: device_temperature_celsius
metrics.description: This metric reports the temperature reading of each Huawei hardware sensor (HUAWEI-ENTITY-EXTENT-MIB hwEntityTemperature), in degrees Celsius. Abnormally high temperatures may indicate fan failure, blocked airflow, or excessive ambient heat, and can trigger thermal protection or hardware damage if left unaddressed.

metrics.name: device_fan_state
metrics.description: This metric reports the operational state of each Huawei cooling fan (HUAWEI-ENTITY-EXTENT-MIB hwEntityFanState). Huawei reports a binary state where 1 means normal and 2 means abnormal; any value other than normal indicates a cooling fault that can quickly lead to overheating and should be investigated immediately.

metrics.name: device_optical_rx_power
metrics.description: Per-module SFP/optical receive power in dBm (HUAWEI-ENTITY-EXTENT-MIB hwEntityOpticalRxPower). The device reports µW; Telegraf stores raw µW and this query converts with 10*log10(µW/1000), dropping <=0 (invalid/no-module). Dimension descr is entPhysicalName. A dropping RX level is an early sign of fiber attenuation, dirty optics, or a failing peer transmitter.

metrics.name: device_optical_tx_power
metrics.description: Per-module SFP/optical transmit power in dBm (HUAWEI-ENTITY-EXTENT-MIB hwEntityOpticalTxPower). The device reports µW; Telegraf stores raw µW and this query converts with 10*log10(µW/1000), dropping <=0 (invalid/no-module). Dimension descr is entPhysicalName. An abnormally low TX level indicates a failing laser/optic rather than fiber attenuation alone.

metrics.name: interface_ifHCInOctets
metrics.description: This metric indicates the average rate of bytes received over the past 5 minutes, measured in bytes per second, from the 64-bit IF-MIB ifHCInOctets counter (ifXTable). The 64-bit counter avoids the rapid wrap of the 32-bit ifInOctets on high-speed switch ports, keeping the rate accurate.

metrics.name: interface_ifHCOutOctets
metrics.description: This metric calculates the average rate of bytes sent over the past 5 minutes, measured in bytes per second, from the 64-bit IF-MIB ifHCOutOctets counter (ifXTable). The 64-bit counter avoids the rapid wrap of the 32-bit ifOutOctets on high-speed switch ports, keeping the rate accurate.

metrics.name: snmp_uptime
metrics.description: This metric indicates the uptime of the device since the last restart. By monitoring the uptime, network administrators can understand the stability and reliability of the device and identify potential reboot or failure issues.
